Summary  
Data source overview: The excerpt from the Effective Altruism Foundation’s research agenda (section 7) surveys open theoretical problems in decision-theoretic foundations for Transformative AI (TAI). It highlights how computational boundedness, logical uncertainty, model misspecification and the limitations of causal decision theory (CDT) can undermine cooperation among future AI systems, and argues for developing bounded and acausal decision theories (e.g., Functional Decision Theory, evidential cooperation) as remedies. Although the text is largely conceptual, it implicitly proposes interventions at the agent-design stage.  

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[78] – The paper is theoretical and does not spell out engineering details, so several intervention nodes are moderately inferred (confidence penalties reflected in edge scores). The JSON has been hand-checked for naming consistency, connectivity and structural validity.  

Instruction-set improvement: Including short examples of how to treat purely theoretical papers (with no empirical validation) would reduce ambiguity about the “validation evidence” category and acceptable inference levels. Explicit guidance on acceptable abstraction levels for risks (e.g., whether “cooperation failure” or “misalignment” is too broad) would further standardise node naming.  

Inference strategy justification: Interventions were inferred by translating each design recommendation or research priority into an explicit action that an AI-safety engineer could take at model-design time. Edges deriving from such inference are marked with confidence 2.  

Extraction completeness: All causal chains from risks → problem analyses → theoretical insights → design rationales → implementation mechanisms → validation evidence → interventions that are either explicitly stated or strongly implied have been captured and interconnected; no isolated nodes remain.  

Key limitations:  
1. Validation evidence is largely theoretical; real empirical results are absent.  
2. Only high-level implementation detail is available; deeper algorithmic specifics would refine intervention granularity.  
3. Some edge confidences are necessarily low due to conceptual rather than empirical support.
